data_quality.summary: Fertilizer rates are guidance drawn from Kenyan government, KALRO, IFDC and Ministry sources. They are not a prescription: a soil test is the right basis for a real recommendation.
notes: Kenya has no single national rate per crop. Government maize recommendations are made at sub-county level (NAAIAP/KARI 2014) and are not summarised here.

IFDC Fertilizer Use Optimizer (FUO) programmes depend on region, yield goal and budget. Their rates differ by large factors (for example maize DAP 11 to 81 kg per acre), so each is labelled with its region and budget level.
Each reported figure is stored as the source gave it ('reported'); per-acre, per-hectare and nutrient amounts are derived by code and re-checked by validate_fertilizers.py.
Where a source gave a choice of products (for example urea or CAN), both are listed under 'alternatives'.
CAN is sold in 21, 26 and 27 percent N grades; calculations here use 26 percent. Check the bag label.
Bottle-top measures are not used because tops differ: IFDC calibrates a soda-bottle top at about 3.5 g of DAP or CAN, while the Ministry guide treats a half-litre water-bottle top as 5 g.
Programmes marked legacy_not_advised are included so the app can recognise common practice, not to recommend it.
Crops with status not_yet_sourced have no rates on purpose: no Kenyan source was retrieved, and inventing numbers could cost farmers money.

program_status_values.general_default: Usable as a general starting point.

budget_levels.higher: Above the lowest level; the exact level is not stated in the retrieved text.

units.note: 1 hectare = 2.4711 acres; per-acre rates are multiplied by 2.4711 to give per-hectare rates.

nutrient_conversion.formula: product kg = nutrient kg / (percent of nutrient in product / 100)
nutrient_conversion.example: To supply 59.6 kg P2O5 from DAP (46 percent P2O5): 59.6 / 0.46 = 129.6 kg DAP. DAP also supplies nitrogen (18 percent), so count it before adding CAN or urea.

products.name: DAP (diammonium phosphate)
products.notes: Most widely used basal fertilizer in Kenya. Mix well with soil so it does not scorch seed or seedlings. Government maize recommendations treat DAP as the most acidifying common fertilizer.

products.name: Urea
products.notes: Concentrated nitrogen; second most used top-dress after CAN.

products.name: CAN (calcium ammonium nitrate)
products.notes: Most used top-dress fertilizer in Kenya. Bags are sold in different grades: check the bag label, because nitrogen content may be 21, 26 or 27 percent and the calculation depends on it.

evidence.basis: KALRO nutrient chart (21 and 26 percent); ICL trial sheet (27 percent)

products.name: Ammonium sulphate (SA)
products.notes: Supplies sulphur as well as nitrogen. Used as an alternative top-dress; the Ministry chili handout suggests it in place of CAN on alkaline soils.

products.name: TSP (triple superphosphate)
products.notes: Phosphorus without nitrogen. Government maize guidance regards TSP and SSP as non-acidifying, so TSP is preferred over DAP on acid soils.

products.name: MOP (muriate of potash)
products.notes: Potassium source (also called KCl). Potassium is not needed on every soil: use a soil test.

evidence.basis: Standard commercial grade; the 60 percent K2O figure is not stated in the retrieved Kenyan sources

products.name: NPK 23:23:0
products.notes: Common basal fertilizer, a no-potassium alternative to DAP.

products.name: NPK 17:17:17
products.notes: Balanced compound; also used for coffee, banana and vegetables.

products.name: Mavuno planting fertilizer (NPK 10:26:10)
products.notes: Compound with added calcium, magnesium, sulphur and trace elements. Government maize guidance treats it as less acidifying than DAP.

products.name: NPKS 25:5:5:5 (tea fertilizer)
products.notes: Standard tea fertilizer. In a long-term KALRO trial it acidified the soil more than NPK 20:10:10, with no yield difference.

products.name: NPK 20:10:10
products.notes: Alternative tea fertilizer and also sold for coffee. Gave the same tea yields as 25:5:5:5 and left more soil P and K.

evidence.basis: KALRO Tea Research Institute; AGRA/IFDC report

products.name: NPK 26:5:5
products.notes: Older standard tea fertilizer, used as the control in KALRO blended-fertilizer trials.

products.name: Calcium nitrate
products.notes: Top-dress for fruits and vegetables; calcium helps against blossom-end rot in tomatoes.

products.name: Farmyard manure
products.notes: Nutrient content varies widely. Use only thoroughly decomposed manure (fresh manure can bring cutworms). Replaces part of the fertilizer: KALRO publishes equivalence tables (see F3), not yet transcribed here.

products.name: Agricultural lime
products.notes: Raises pH and removes aluminium toxicity. Rates are in tonnes per hectare and depend on a lab test. Do not use on tea or on soils that are already neutral or alkaline.

lime.when_to_lime: Lime if soil pH is more than 0.2 units below the crop's pH requirement (KALRO / IFDC).
lime.why: Below about pH 5.5 aluminium becomes toxic to plants and phosphorus is poorly available. About 13 percent of Kenya's land (about 7.5 million ha, 29 counties) is acid.

lab_formula.text: Lime requirement (t/ha) = 16.988 - 2.722 x Mehlich buffer pH
lab_formula.warning: Requires a lab-measured Mehlich buffer pH; do not use an ordinary soil pH reading.

lime.trial_note: From a One Acre Fund trial in western Kenya; micro-dosing is under evaluation and is not yet a standard recommendation.
cautions: Do not lime tea soils.
Do not lime neutral or alkaline soils.
Lime is bulky and powdery: apply on a calm day and mix into the soil.
Use ordinary soil pH to decide whether to test; use the lab test to decide how much.

application_guidance.text: Mix DAP thoroughly with the soil so it does not scorch seeds or seedlings.
Place or band fertilizer next to the plants rather than broadcasting where the source says so; it is more effective and economical.
Apply top-dressing around the base of the plant and cover with soil; do not put fertilizer directly on the plant.
Use only thoroughly decomposed manure; fresh manure can introduce cutworms.
On acid soils use TSP, manure or a less acidifying compound instead of repeated DAP.
Always base the actual amount on a soil test where possible; the rates in this file are general.

soil_guidance.basis: Derived by fixed rules from soil.json (typical pH, drainage, texture, limiting factors); general agronomic reasoning, not a Kenyan trial result.

guidance: Soil is neutral to alkaline. Do not lime; high pH can lock up phosphorus and micronutrients.
The soil can be waterlogged: apply nitrogen when the soil is not saturated and improve drainage.
Salinity or sodicity is a concern: fertilizer will not fix it; address drainage and water quality first.
